title: First Code of Justinian promulgated
note: Justinian issued the first edition of his consolidated code of imperial law, which went on to underpin much of later European civil law.

title: Hagia Sophia dedicated by Justinian
note: The rebuilt Great Church of Constantinople was consecrated less than six years after the Nika riots destroyed its predecessor.

title: Second Council of Constantinople opens
note: The fifth ecumenical council met to condemn the Three Chapters and continued sitting until 2 June 553.

title: Third Council of Toledo opens; Visigoths renounce Arianism
note: King Reccared and the Visigothic nobility formally embraced Catholic Christianity at this council; some sources give 8 May for the opening.

title: Gregory the Great consecrated Bishop of Rome
note: Gregory, elected after Pelagius II died of plague, was consecrated and later sent the mission of Augustine to the English.

title: Hijra: Muhammad arrives at Quba near Medina
note: Tradition dates the arrival to Monday 8 Rabi al-Awwal; Julian conversions vary by a few days (20 to 24 September), while the Islamic era itself is counted from 16 July 622.

title: Battle of Badr
note: The Muslims of Medina defeated a larger Meccan force on 17 Ramadan AH 2; the Julian date is a calendar conversion.

title: Death of Muhammad in Medina
note: Muhammad died in Medina, and Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph.

title: Battle of Yarmouk ends in Arab victory
note: The decisive day of a battle lasting several days, in which Rashidun forces broke Byzantine power in Syria.

title: Third Council of Constantinople opens
note: The sixth ecumenical council, held in the domed Trullus hall of the palace, condemned Monothelitism.

title: Battle of Karbala; Husayn ibn Ali killed
note: Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, was killed on 10 Muharram AH 61, remembered every year at Ashura.

title: Battle of Tours (Poitiers)
note: Charles Martel's Franks stopped an Umayyad army; the 10 October date is traditional and some scholars prefer 733.

title: Boniface martyred at Dokkum
note: The English missionary bishop who evangelised much of Germany was killed with companions in Frisia; 5 June is his feast and traditional death day.

title: An Lushan Rebellion begins
note: An Lushan marched out of Fanyang against the Tang court, starting a war that devastated the dynasty.

title: Second Council of Nicaea opens
note: The seventh ecumenical council restored the veneration of icons, setting out its definition on 13 October.

title: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
note: Norse raiders sacked the island monastery, usually taken as the start of the Viking Age; one chronicle copy says 8 January instead.

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor in Rome
note: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king emperor of the Romans at Christmas Mass in St Peter's.

title: Charter founding the Abbey of Cluny
note: Duke William of Aquitaine endowed a monastery free of lay control, which became the centre of a major monastic reform; some date the charter to 909.

title: Otto I crowned emperor
note: Pope John XII crowned Otto in Rome, founding what came to be called the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Battle of Clontarf
note: Brian Boru defeated Leinster and Norse forces on Good Friday but was killed in the fighting.

title: Humbert lays excommunication on Hagia Sophia altar
note: The papal legate placed a bull against Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar, the act usually taken as the start of the East-West Schism.

title: Battle of Hastings
note: William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II, opening the Norman Conquest.

title: William the Conqueror crowned at Westminster
note: William was crowned king on Christmas Day in Westminster Abbey.

title: Battle of Manzikert
note: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated and captured Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

title: Henry IV absolved at Canossa
note: After standing as a penitent at the castle gate, the excommunicated king was absolved by Pope Gregory VII.

title: Urban II calls the First Crusade at Clermont
note: Pope Urban II preached in a field outside Clermont, urging Christians to go to the aid of the East and to Jerusalem.

title: First Crusade captures Jerusalem
note: Crusaders broke into the city after a siege of about five weeks and massacred many of its inhabitants.

title: Concordat of Worms
note: Emperor Henry V and Pope Callixtus II settled the Investiture Controversy over who appoints bishops.

title: Thomas Becket murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
note: Four knights of Henry II killed the archbishop in his cathedral, and he was canonised within three years.

title: Battle of Hattin
note: Saladin destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near Tiberias, opening the way to Jerusalem.

title: Saladin takes Jerusalem
note: The city surrendered to Saladin after a short siege, ending 88 years of crusader rule.

title: Fourth Crusade storms Constantinople
note: Crusaders broke into the Christian capital and sacked it over three days, deepening the split between East and West.

title: Magna Carta sealed at Runnymede
note: King John agreed to the charter of liberties put to him by rebel barons.

title: Fourth Lateran Council opens
note: Innocent III's great council defined transubstantiation and required annual confession and communion.

title: Honorius III approves the Dominican Order
note: The bull Religiosam vitam confirmed Dominic's community of preachers at Toulouse.

title: Franciscan Rule approved by papal bull
note: Honorius III confirmed the final Rule of Francis of Assisi with the bull Solet annuere.

title: Abbasid caliph surrenders Baghdad to Hulagu
note: Caliph al-Musta'sim surrendered to the Mongols, who began sacking the city three days later.

title: Battle of Ain Jalut
note: The Mamluks of Egypt defeated a Mongol army in Galilee, halting the Mongol advance toward Egypt.

title: Boniface VIII proclaims the first Jubilee
note: The bull Antiquorum habet offered a plenary indulgence to pilgrims to Rome and began the Holy Year tradition.

title: Battle of Bannockburn
note: Robert the Bruce defeated Edward II on the second day of the battle, securing Scottish independence for a generation.

title: Declaration of Arbroath
note: Scottish nobles wrote to Pope John XXII asserting Scotland's independence and asking him to recognise Robert the Bruce as king.

title: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming dynasty
note: At Nanjing, Zhu proclaimed himself emperor as the Hongwu Emperor, and his forces drove the Mongol Yuan from Beijing later that year.

title: Blackfriars 'Earthquake Synod' condemns Wycliffe
note: Archbishop Courtenay's council condemned Wycliffe's teachings while an earthquake shook London.

title: Jan Hus burned at Constance
note: The Czech reformer was condemned by the Council of Constance and executed despite a promise of safe conduct.

title: Battle of Agincourt
note: Henry V's outnumbered English army, relying on its longbowmen, defeated the French on St Crispin's Day.

title: Martin V elected, ending the Western Schism
note: The Council of Constance chose Oddone Colonna as the single pope, closing nearly forty years of rival papacies.

title: Joan of Arc burned at Rouen
note: After a church trial under English control, Joan was burned as a relapsed heretic; she was cleared in 1456 and canonised in 1920.

title: Council of Florence decrees union with the Greeks
note: The decree Laetentur caeli announced a reunion of the Latin and Greek churches, which was later rejected in the East.

title: Fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans
note: Mehmed II's army stormed the walls, ending the Byzantine Empire, and Hagia Sophia became a mosque.

title: Mainz Psalter completed, first dated printed book
note: Fust and Schoeffer's colophon dates the book to the eve of the Assumption and is the first to name its printers and date.

title: Kongo king Nzinga a Nkuwu baptised as Joao I
note: The king and his family received baptism from Portuguese priests, beginning Kongo's long Catholic history.

title: Granada surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella
note: Emir Muhammad XII handed over the city, ending the last Muslim state in Iberia.

title: Alhambra Decree expels Jews from Spain
note: The Catholic Monarchs ordered all practising Jews to convert or leave their kingdoms by the end of July.

title: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas
note: Columbus's expedition reached an island the Lucayans called Guanahani; the date is Julian (21 October in the proleptic Gregorian).

title: Treaty of Tordesillas
note: Spain and Portugal divided newly found lands outside Europe along a meridian west of the Cape Verde islands.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
note: Da Gama's fleet arrived on the Malabar coast, opening a sea route from Europe to India around Africa.

title: Savonarola executed in Florence
note: The Dominican preacher who had dominated Florence was hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria.

title: Cabral's fleet sights Brazil
note: A Portuguese fleet bound for India sighted Monte Pascoal and claimed the land for Portugal.

title: Montesinos preaches against abuse of the Taino
note: On the fourth Sunday of Advent the Dominican Antonio de Montesinos denounced the colonists' treatment of the native people.

title: Complutensian Polyglot New Testament completed
note: The colophon of Cardinal Cisneros's polyglot dates the first printed Greek New Testament, though the work was not issued until about 1522.

title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
note: Luther sent his theses against indulgences to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz; the posting on the Wittenberg church door is traditional.

title: Luther burns the papal bull Exsurge Domine
note: Outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate, Luther burned the bull threatening him with excommunication, along with books of canon law.

title: Luther refuses to recant at the Diet of Worms
note: Before Emperor Charles V, Luther declined to retract his writings unless refuted by Scripture and plain reason.

title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
note: Cuauhtemoc was captured and the Aztec capital fell to Cortes and his Tlaxcalan and other Indigenous allies after a long siege.

title: Victoria returns, completing first circumnavigation
note: Elcano brought the last ship of Magellan's expedition into Sanlucar de Barrameda with 18 survivors.

title: First believers' baptisms in Zurich
note: Conrad Grebel baptised George Blaurock at Felix Manz's house, usually taken as the founding of the Anabaptist movement.

title: First Battle of Panipat
note: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi of the Delhi Sultanate and founded the Mughal Empire.

title: Battle of Mohacs
note: Suleiman the Magnificent destroyed the Hungarian army, and King Louis II died fleeing the field.

title: Schleitheim Confession adopted
note: Swiss Brethren meeting under Michael Sattler agreed seven articles that defined early Anabaptist practice.

title: Augsburg Confession presented to Charles V
note: The Lutheran princes had Melanchthon's statement of faith read aloud at the Diet of Augsburg.

title: Our Lady of Guadalupe image revealed (tradition)
note: Catholic tradition holds that Juan Diego showed Bishop Zumarraga the image on his cloak on this day; early documentation is debated.

title: Pizarro captures Atahualpa at Cajamarca
note: Spanish forces ambushed the Inca ruler's retinue in Cajamarca's plaza and took him prisoner.

title: Coverdale Bible finished printing
note: The colophon of Myles Coverdale's translation, the first complete printed English Bible, gives 4 October 1535.

title: William Tyndale executed at Vilvoorde
note: The translator of the English New Testament was strangled and burned for heresy; 6 October is the traditional date.

title: Paul III issues Sublimis Deus
note: The bull declared that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas were rational beings who must not be enslaved or robbed.

title: Society of Jesus approved by Paul III
note: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's order.

title: Battle of Wayna Daga
note: Emperor Gelawdewos and Portuguese musketeers defeated and killed Ahmad Gran, saving the Christian Ethiopian kingdom; sources differ on the date.

title: Council of Trent opens
note: The council that framed the Catholic response to the Reformation held its first session.

title: First Book of Common Prayer comes into use
note: Cranmer's English liturgy became mandatory on Whitsunday, sparking the Prayer Book Rebellion in the West Country.

title: Francis Xavier lands at Kagoshima
note: The Jesuit missionary came ashore with Japanese convert Anjiro, beginning Christian missions in Japan.

title: Peace of Augsburg
note: The settlement let each prince of the Empire choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his own territory.

title: Scottish Parliament approves the Scots Confession
note: The Reformation Parliament adopted the Reformed confession drafted by John Knox and five colleagues.

title: Battle of Lepanto
note: The Holy League's galleys destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet in the Gulf of Patras.

title: St Bartholomew's Day massacre begins
note: Catholic mobs and royal troops in Paris killed Huguenot leaders and thousands of Protestants, and the killing spread to other cities.

title: Oda Nobunaga dies at Honno-ji
note: Akechi Mitsuhide's troops attacked the Kyoto temple and Nobunaga took his own life; this is a Julian conversion of the Japanese date (Tensho 10, 6th month, 2nd day).

title: Gregorian calendar takes effect
note: Following Gregory XIII's bull Inter gravissimas, Catholic lands went straight from Thursday 4 October to Friday 15 October.

title: Battle of Gravelines breaks the Spanish Armada
note: English fireships and guns scattered the Armada off Flanders; this is the English Old Style date, and the Spanish recorded 8 August (New Style).

title: Battle of Tondibi
note: A Moroccan army armed with firearms defeated Askia Ishaq II, bringing about the collapse of the Songhai Empire.

title: Edict of Nantes
note: Henry IV gave French Protestants legal toleration and civil rights, ending the Wars of Religion.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
note: Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory led to the Tokugawa shogunate; this is a conversion of the Japanese date (Keicho 5, 9th month, 15th day).

title: Matteo Ricci enters Beijing
note: The Jesuit missionary arrived at the Ming capital and was later allowed to stay there under the Wanli Emperor's patronage.

title: English colonists land at Jamestown
note: The Virginia Company settlers came ashore on the James River and built James Fort; the date is Old Style (24 May New Style).

title: Champlain founds Quebec
note: Samuel de Champlain set up his habitation at the narrows of the St Lawrence, the start of Quebec City.

title: Defenestration of Prague
note: Protestant nobles threw two Catholic imperial regents and their secretary from a window of Prague Castle, triggering the Thirty Years' War.

title: Synod of Dort opens
note: The international Reformed synod at Dordrecht answered the Remonstrants and produced the Canons of Dort, closing on 9 May 1619.

title: Mayflower Compact signed
note: At anchor off Cape Cod, the Pilgrims and other passengers agreed to form a civil body politic; the date is Old Style (21 November New Style).

title: Ville-Marie (Montreal) founded
note: Maisonneuve and about fifty settlers founded a missionary colony on the island of Montreal.

title: Peace of Westphalia signed
note: The treaties of Munster and Osnabruck ended the Thirty Years' War and recognised Calvinism alongside Lutheranism and Catholicism in the Empire.

title: Execution of Charles I
note: The king was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall; contemporaries wrote 1648 because their year began on 25 March, and the New Style date is 9 February.

title: Pascal's 'night of fire'
note: Blaise Pascal recorded an intense religious experience on a parchment he kept sewn into his coat until he died.

title: The Great Ejection
note: About two thousand ministers who would not conform to the Act of Uniformity lost their livings on St Bartholomew's Day (3 September New Style).

title: Battle of Mbwila
note: Portuguese forces from Luanda defeated and killed King Antonio I of Kongo, setting off decades of civil war in the kingdom.

title: Great Fire of London begins
note: A fire in a bakery on Pudding Lane burned for four days and destroyed most of the medieval City, including old St Paul's (12 September New Style).

title: Edict of Fontainebleau revokes Nantes
note: Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship, and roughly 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad.

title: William of Orange lands at Torbay
note: William's landing at Brixham began the Glorious Revolution that removed James II; the date is Old Style (15 November New Style).

title: Toleration Act receives royal assent
note: The Act allowed Protestant dissenters who took certain oaths to worship freely in licensed meeting houses (3 June New Style).

title: Battle of the Boyne
note: William III defeated James II near Drogheda; the date is Old Style (11 July New Style), and the battle is now marked on 12 July.

title: Peter the Great founds Saint Petersburg
note: Work began on the Peter and Paul Fortress on Hare Island in the Neva; Russia used the Julian calendar, and the New Style date is 27 May.

title: Ziegenbalg and Plutschau land at Tranquebar
note: The first Protestant missionaries to India arrived at the Danish colony, and Ziegenbalg later translated the New Testament into Tamil.

title: Moravian refugees found Herrnhut
note: Christian David felled the first tree for a settlement on Count Zinzendorf's estate, which became the centre of the renewed Moravian Church.

title: Moravian 'Pentecost' at Berthelsdorf
note: A communion service brought renewal and reconciliation to the Herrnhut community, followed by a century-long round-the-clock prayer watch.

title: First Moravian missionaries reach St Thomas
note: Leonhard Dober and David Nitschmann arrived in the Danish West Indies to preach to enslaved Africans.

title: John Wesley's Aldersgate experience
note: Listening to Luther's preface to Romans read aloud, Wesley felt his heart 'strangely warmed' (4 June New Style).

title: Whitefield's first open-air sermon at Kingswood
note: Whitefield preached in the open air to coal miners near Bristol, a key step in the field preaching of the Evangelical Revival; contemporaries wrote 1738/9 (28 February New Style).

title: Edwards preaches 'Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God'
note: Jonathan Edwards's sermon at Enfield became the best-known sermon of the Great Awakening (19 July New Style).

title: Premiere of Handel's Messiah in Dublin
note: The oratorio was first performed at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street as a charity benefit (24 April New Style).

title: Battle of Culloden
note: Government forces crushed Charles Edward Stuart's Jacobite army near Inverness (27 April New Style).

title: Halifax founded by Edward Cornwallis
note: Cornwallis arrived at Chebucto with settlers to found Halifax, on land the Mi'kmaq had not ceded; this is the Old Style date (2 July New Style).

title: Britain and its colonies adopt the Gregorian calendar
note: Under the Calendar Act, Wednesday 2 September was followed by Thursday 14 September, and the legal year already began on 1 January.

title: Expulsion order read to the Acadians at Grand-Pre
note: Lt Col John Winslow read the deportation order to Acadian men gathered in the Grand-Pre church.

title: Great Lisbon earthquake
note: On All Saints' morning an earthquake, tsunami and fires destroyed most of Lisbon and shook European theology and philosophy.

title: Battle of Plassey
note: Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah, starting British rule in Bengal.

title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
note: Wolfe's British army defeated Montcalm's outside Quebec, and both generals were mortally wounded.

title: Fall of Ayutthaya
note: Burmese forces breached the walls after a 14-month siege and destroyed the Siamese capital.

title: Boston Tea Party
note: Colonists protesting the Tea Act dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor.

title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
note: Fighting between British regulars and colonial militia began the American Revolutionary War.

title: Declaration of Independence adopted
note: The Continental Congress in Philadelphia approved the final text declaring the thirteen colonies independent.

title: Christmas Conference founds American Methodism
note: Preachers meeting at Lovely Lane Chapel in Baltimore organised the Methodist Episcopal Church and chose Asbury and Coke as superintendents.

title: First Fleet at Sydney Cove
note: Arthur Phillip raised the British flag at Sydney Cove, founding the convict colony of New South Wales on Aboriginal land.

title: George Washington inaugurated
note: Washington took the oath as the first President of the United States at Federal Hall.

title: Storming of the Bastille
note: A Paris crowd seized the royal fortress-prison, a defining moment of the French Revolution.

title: Bois Caiman ceremony
note: A nighttime gathering of enslaved people led by Dutty Boukman preceded the uprising that began the Haitian Revolution; the exact date rests on later accounts.

title: Baptist Missionary Society founded at Kettering
note: Twelve Baptist ministers, urged on by William Carey, formed the society in Widow Wallis's parlour, launching the modern missionary movement.

title: Execution of Louis XVI
note: The deposed king was guillotined in the Place de la Revolution after the Convention convicted him of treason.

title: William Carey arrives in Bengal
note: Carey and John Thomas reached Calcutta on a Danish ship after five months at sea; some accounts give 12 November.

title: Church Missionary Society founded
note: Evangelical Anglicans of the Clapham circle formed the society at the Castle and Falcon inn in London to send missionaries to Africa and the East.

title: Rosetta Stone discovered
note: French soldiers found the stele at Rashid, and its parallel texts later allowed hieroglyphs to be deciphered; accounts differ between 15 and 19 July.
